dati_metodo: About 1,695-2,581 first-round US VC contracts (2002-2015 sample), dynamic search-and-matching structural model estimated with selection correction

righe.estrazione: The txt does not model or show investors trading valuation against contract terms. It shows (structural search-and-matching model) that higher-quality VCs offer more investor-friendly terms, which lower firm value, but the entrepreneur accepts them because VC quality raises startup value: the trade is terms versus VC quality. On valuation, it only says post-money valuation is a poor metric of firm value because it ignores terms other than the equity share, and proposes a term-adjusted valuation (about 15.7% lower in one example).
righe.citazione: startup’s value increases with VC quality, and this value
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Seed/first-round contracts 2002-2015, structural model; no round-to-round valuation step.
righe.note: The tesi is not contradicted but not supported: no passage says valuation is traded against terms. Closest points: terms traded against VC quality; post-money valuation ignores terms (Metrick and Yasuda 2010 and Gornall and Strebulaev 2020 are cited for this, the txt reuses it). A possible narrower tesi: post-money valuation is a poor measure of firm value when contract terms differ.
